paragraphs: Children in care in Thurrock, including Grays, Tilbury, Purfleet, Chafford Hundred and Stanford-le-Hope, are looked after by Thurrock Council's own fostering service and by the independent agencies listed on this page. In May 2026 the council said it had 68 foster carers and urgently needed more, so that children can stay near their schools, friends and communities. A year earlier it pointed to a shortage of 440 foster carers across the East of England.

There is no single type of foster carer: the council welcomes people who are single or in a relationship, working or retired, and says the key requirement is a safe, caring and stable home. Respite fostering, giving a child and their regular carers a short break, is one of the ways people get involved.

Thurrock publishes its rates in full. From April 2026 its weekly total for each child, combining the child's maintenance and the carer's reward payment, runs from £415 for a child aged up to 4 to £516 for a young person aged 16 or over at the standard Care Skills rate, and from £467 to £568 at the Care Skills+ rate for children with more complex needs. Carers also receive birthday and festival payments and a paid break of up to four weeks a year, and those who live in Thurrock and foster for the council are exempt from council tax. Our Thurrock allowance page has the full table.
As agencies set their own fees and support, it is worth comparing the council's offer with two or three of the services below.
